14 /-!
15 # Basic definitions about topological spaces
16 
17 This file contains definitions about topology that do not require imports
18 other than `Mathlib/Data/Set/Lattice.lean`.
19 
20 ## Main definitions
21 
22 * `TopologicalSpace X`: a typeclass endowing `X` with a topology.
23   By definition, a topology is a collection of sets called *open sets* such that
24 
25   - `isOpen_univ`: the whole space is open;
26   - `IsOpen.inter`: the intersection of two open sets is an open set;
27   - `isOpen_sUnion`: the union of a family of open sets is an open set.
28 
29 * `IsOpen s`: predicate saying that `s` is an open set, same as `TopologicalSpace.IsOpen`.
30 
31 * `IsClosed s`: a set is called *closed*, if its complement is an open set.
32   For technical reasons, this is a typeclass.
33 
34 * `IsClopen s`: a set is *clopen* if it is both closed and open.
35 
36 * `interior s`: the *interior* of a set `s` is the maximal open set that is included in `s`.
37 
38 * `closure s`: the *closure* of a set `s` is the minimal closed set that includes `s`.
39 
40 * `frontier s`: the *frontier* of a set is the set difference `closure s \ interior s`.
41   A point `x` belongs to `frontier s`, if any neighborhood of `x`
42   contains points both from `s` and `sᶜ`.
43 
44 * `Dense s`: a set is *dense* if its closure is the whole space.
45   We define it as `∀ x, x ∈ closure s` so that one can write `(h : Dense s) x`.
46 
47 * `DenseRange f`: a function has *dense range*, if `Set.range f` is a dense set.
48 
49 * `Continuous f`: a map is *continuous*, if the preimage of any open set is an open set.
50 
51 * `IsOpenMap f`: a map is an *open map*, if the image of any open set is an open set.
52 
53 * `IsClosedMap f`: a map is a *closed map*, if the image of any closed set is a closed set.
54 
55 ** Notation
56 
57 We introduce notation `IsOpen[t]`, `IsClosed[t]`, `closure[t]`, `Continuous[t₁, t₂]`
58 that allow passing custom topologies to these predicates and functions without using `@`.
59 -/
60 
61 @[expose] public section
62 
63 assert_not_exists Monoid
64 
65 universe u v
66 open Set
67 
68 /-- A topology on `X`. -/
69 class TopologicalSpace (X : Type u) where
70   /-- A predicate saying that a set is an open set. Use `IsOpen` in the root namespace instead. -/
71   protected IsOpen : Set X → Prop
72   /-- The set representing the whole space is an open set.
73   Use `isOpen_univ` in the root namespace instead. -/
74   protected isOpen_univ : IsOpen univ
75   /-- The intersection of two open sets is an open set. Use `IsOpen.inter` instead. -/
76   protected isOpen_inter : ∀ s t, IsOpen s → IsOpen t → IsOpen (s ∩ t)
77   /-- The union of a family of open sets is an open set.
78   Use `isOpen_sUnion` in the root namespace instead. -/
79   protected isOpen_sUnion : ∀ s, (∀ t ∈ s, IsOpen t) → IsOpen (⋃₀ s)
80 
81 variable {X : Type u} {Y : Type v}
82 
83 /-! ### Predicates on sets -/
84 
85 section Defs
86 
87 variable [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {s t : Set X}
88 
89 /-- `IsOpen s` means that `s` is open in the ambient topological space on `X` -/
90 def IsOpen : Set X → Prop := TopologicalSpace.IsOpen
91 
92 @[simp] theorem isOpen_univ : IsOpen (univ : Set X) := TopologicalSpace.isOpen_univ
93 
94 theorem IsOpen.inter (hs : IsOpen s) (ht : IsOpen t) : IsOpen (s ∩ t) :=
95   TopologicalSpace.isOpen_inter s t hs ht
96 
97 theorem isOpen_sUnion {s : Set (Set X)} (h : ∀ t ∈ s, IsOpen t) : IsOpen (⋃₀ s) :=
98   TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion s h
99 
100 /-- A set is closed if its complement is open -/
101 class IsClosed (s : Set X) : Prop where
102   /-- The complement of a closed set is an open set. -/
103   isOpen_compl : IsOpen sᶜ
104 
105 /-- A set is clopen if it is both closed and open. -/
106 def IsClopen (s : Set X) : Prop :=
107   IsClosed s ∧ IsOpen s
108 
109 /--
110 A set is locally closed if it is the intersection of some open set and some closed set.
111 Also see `isLocallyClosed_tfae` and other lemmas in `Mathlib/Topology/LocallyClosed.lean`.
112 -/
113 def IsLocallyClosed (s : Set X) : Prop := ∃ (U Z : Set X), IsOpen U ∧ IsClosed Z ∧ s = U ∩ Z
114 
115 /-- The interior of a set `s` is the largest open subset of `s`. -/
116 def interior (s : Set X) : Set X :=
117   ⋃₀ { t | IsOpen t ∧ t ⊆ s }
118 
119 /-- The closure of `s` is the smallest closed set containing `s`. -/
120 def closure (s : Set X) : Set X :=
121   ⋂₀ { t | IsClosed t ∧ s ⊆ t }
122 
123 /-- The frontier of a set is the set of points between the closure and interior. -/
124 def frontier (s : Set X) : Set X :=
125   closure s \ interior s
126 
127 /--
128 The coborder is defined as the complement of `closure s \ s`,
129 or the union of `s` and the complement of `∂(s)`.
130 This is the largest set in which `s` is closed, and `s` is locally closed if and only if
131 `coborder s` is open.
132 
133 This is unnamed in the literature, and this name is due to the fact that `coborder s = (border sᶜ)ᶜ`
134 where `border s = s \ interior s` is the border in the sense of Hausdorff.
135 -/
136 def coborder (s : Set X) : Set X :=
137   (closure s \ s)ᶜ
138 
139 /-- A set is dense in a topological space if every point belongs to its closure. -/
140 def Dense (s : Set X) : Prop :=
141   ∀ x, x ∈ closure s
142 
143 /-- `f : α → X` has dense range if its range (image) is a dense subset of `X`. -/
144 def DenseRange {α : Type*} (f : α → X) := Dense (range f)
145 
146 /-- A function between topological spaces is continuous if the preimage
147   of every open set is open. Registered as a structure to make sure it is not unfolded by Lean. -/
148 @[fun_prop]
149 structure Continuous (f : X → Y) : Prop where
150   /-- The preimage of an open set under a continuous function is an open set. Use `IsOpen.preimage`
151   instead. -/
152   isOpen_preimage : ∀ s, IsOpen s → IsOpen (f ⁻¹' s)
153 
154 /-- A map `f : X → Y` is said to be an *open map*,
155 if the image of any open `U : Set X` is open in `Y`. -/
156 def IsOpenMap (f : X → Y) : Prop := ∀ U : Set X, IsOpen U → IsOpen (f '' U)
157 
158 /-- A map `f : X → Y` is said to be a *closed map*,
159 if the image of any closed `U : Set X` is closed in `Y`. -/
160 def IsClosedMap (f : X → Y) : Prop := ∀ U : Set X, IsClosed U → IsClosed (f '' U)
161 
162 /-- An open quotient map is an open map `f : X → Y` which is both an open map and a quotient map.
163 Equivalently, it is a surjective continuous open map.
164 We use the latter characterization as a definition.
165 
166 Many important quotient maps are open quotient maps, including
167 
168 - the quotient map from a topological space to its quotient by the action of a group;
169 - the quotient map from a topological group to its quotient by a normal subgroup;
170 - the quotient map from a topological space to its separation quotient.
171 
172 Contrary to general quotient maps,
173 the category of open quotient maps is closed under `Prod.map`.
174 -/
175 @[mk_iff]
176 structure IsOpenQuotientMap (f : X → Y) : Prop where
177   /-- An open quotient map is surjective. -/
178   surjective : Function.Surjective f
179   /-- An open quotient map is continuous. -/
180   continuous : Continuous f
181   /-- An open quotient map is an open map. -/
182   isOpenMap : IsOpenMap f
183 
184 end Defs
185 
186 /-! ### Notation for non-standard topologies -/
187 
188 /-- Notation for `IsOpen` with respect to a non-standard topology. -/
189 scoped[Topology] notation (name := IsOpen_of) "IsOpen[" t "]" => @IsOpen _ t
190 
191 /-- Notation for `IsClosed` with respect to a non-standard topology. -/
192 scoped[Topology] notation (name := IsClosed_of) "IsClosed[" t "]" => @IsClosed _ t
193 
194 /-- Notation for `closure` with respect to a non-standard topology. -/
195 scoped[Topology] notation (name := closure_of) "closure[" t "]" => @closure _ t
196 
197 /-- Notation for `Continuous` with respect to a non-standard topologies. -/
198 scoped[Topology] notation (name := Continuous_of) "Continuous[" t₁ ", " t₂ "]" =>
199   @Continuous _ _ t₁ t₂
200 
201 /-- The property `BaireSpace α` means that the topological space `α` has the Baire property:
202 any countable intersection of open dense subsets is dense.
203 Formulated here when the source space is ℕ.
204 Use `dense_iInter_of_isOpen` which works for any countable index type instead. -/
205 class BaireSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
206   baire_property : ∀ f : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, IsOpen (f n)) → (∀ n, Dense (f n)) → Dense (⋂ n, f n)
